quest.title: Witch's Revelation: Duty's Instruction
quest.description: You encounter Cyno at Barbeloth's fortune-telling booth...
quest.rewards_formatted: Mora x20000, Guide to Admonition x3

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Are you sure you can't make a copy of this card back for me?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hmm... It's very impressive. Maybe we could come to some sort of arrangement...?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Mm, I see. Obtaining beautiful card backs and playing powerful cards both require a certain price. I think I understand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! You don't know why Cyno's here! Maybe he came here to—

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I sure did. That's my buddy, alright — we're on completely the same wavelength!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seriously!?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: There's a small gathering of TCG players taking place here in Fontaine. I heard participants get event-exclusive cardholders for free.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: There were no pressing matters at the Akademiya, so I came over.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even if there were pressing matters, Paimon has a sneaking suspicion you would have found a way to make them... not-so-pressing...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You're right! I managed to finish almost all of my work after only two weeks of overtime.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Sethos helped out, too, so I promised to bring him a cardholder for his trouble. He's very good at paperwork.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Well then, General Mahamatra, are you going to draw a card or not?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Of course. You say this card will predict my future, right?

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Technically, not quite. But it's unlikely to cause much trouble if you choose to understand it that way.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Hm, I see. Is this like that line in "Duel Master"... "Stake your fate on the next card in the draw"?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: And now it's my turn to draw...!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Cyno takes a deep breath, makes a stylish pose, and draws a card...

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Ah, reversed Temperance. A fitting card for the "General Mahamatra" of the Sumeru Akademiya.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You already know who Cyno is?

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Alice mentioned him a few times. She finds it funny that the stuffy old Akademiya has a General Mahamatra with such a "well-developed" sense of humor.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Please thank her for the compliment. Now that I've drawn a card, what should I do next?

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Since it's reversed Temperance, or rather, reversed "Artistry," I suggest you maintain a state of doing nothing for the time being.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: You've been acting rashly and have nearly lost your footing on the narrow bridge of fate.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: It's because I've been playing too much cards, isn't it? Sethos and Tighnari told me the same thing — I've already adjusted my schedule.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: ...I'm not talking about playing cards. I mean your working hours. Surely Genius Invokation TCG isn't the only thing that demands the General Mahamatra's full attention?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: My duties don't leave me much room to adjust them...

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: You're used to bearing the pressure of such a busy schedule alone?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: There are other matras. We share the pressure among us.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: But they all rely on you? Not just the matras, but the researchers and the people of Sumeru... So many people put their faith in you, General Mahamatra.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: They never tell you, perhaps they don't even realize it themselves... Why would they, when they're all so captivated by your unstoppable wit?

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: But you can feel their gazes, looking to you night and day... Oh, and the shadow that walks beside you. He, too, is one of your burdens.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: You're used to leading the way, carrying the burdens of others... I think, perhaps, this is the reason for your imbalance.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I have many friends. One of them just happens to be a "genius" who goes by the name of "Invokation TCG"...

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: So, it seems you have no intention of resting?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: There's no time to rest.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Indeed. For someone such as yourself, if the inner battle is endless, then even death won't mark the end of duty.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: Take this Lunar Arcanum. Perhaps it will lead you to the reason that restores your balance.

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: When it does, the battle within you should also reach a decisive end.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: #Thank you, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: And my thanks to you as well. And don't worry, I promise I won't start acting too crazy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Huh? Why would you... Wait, was that...

response.speaker: Barbeloth
response.text: ...What does this have to do with acting crazy?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Because now I have this card...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...People might accuse me of being a bona-fide "Lunar-tic"!

choices.text: He's come up with another one.
You came all this way to play cards?
